merger_description:
SoftBank Group Corp. (**SBG**) through Tulip Holdco (DE) LLC, proposes to acquire from ABB Ltd (**ABB**), 100% of the shares in ABB Robotics Holdco 1 Ltd (**ABB Robotics**), which at completion, will hold ABB’s robotics division (**the Acquisition**).

SBG is a publicly traded global investor headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, with a large and varied portfolio of investments and subsidiaries focused on the technology sector. Companies and investments of SBG conduct business activities globally across a wide range of sectors, including online learning, mobile and fixed-line communications services, microelectronics, transportation, software-as-a-service, mobile devices, internet advertising and e-commerce, banking, payment and investment, IT platforms, AI, and mobile robots.

ABB Robotics supplies industrial robots including the design, development, manufacturing, sale and service of robotic technologies that help businesses across a wide range of industries. Globally, ABB Robotics’ supplies (i) naked robots (including controllers) and (ii) complete solutions (including functional modules, cells, and systems with various degrees of customisation and integration depending on the customer need). In addition, ABB Robotics also offers the corresponding software, either together with the robots or, to a limited extent, on a stand-alone basis.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is limited horizontal overlap between SBG and ABB
Robotics in the supply of industrial robots in Australia, with
the parties focussed on different product segments
b. the increase in share of supply of industrial robots in
Australia is expected to be small, given the size of the
parties’ operations in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
